inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge whether the Rails-style codebase is organised into the conventional model/controller/view layers with proper extraction.
EVIDENCE: code-files listing under app/ + Gemfile.
SCORE RANGE: 0-5

CRITERIA:
  C1. app/models, app/controllers and app/views are present as separate directories.
  C2. Business logic is extracted into app/services, app/lib or concerns (controllers stay thin; controllers should NOT exceed ~200 LoC each on average).
  C3. db/migrate/ exists and migration filenames follow the timestamped Rails convention.
  C4. Gemfile groups dependencies meaningfully (e.g. group :development/:test/:production blocks).
  C5. Models inherit from a project ApplicationRecord base class (not directly from ActiveRecord::Base).

SCORING ANCHORS:
  - 0 (none):       Fewer than 2 of C1-C5 satisfied; structure is ad-hoc.
  - 2 (basic):      Exactly 2 of C1-C5 satisfied (typically C1 + C3 only).
  - 4 (good):       3 or 4 of C1-C5 satisfied; controllers are mostly thin.
  - 5 (excellent):  All 5 of C1-C5 satisfied; controllers visibly delegate to services/concerns.

OUTPUT: {"score": <0..5>, "reasoning": "<1-3 sentences referencing C1..C5>"}

nodes.description: API design quality: namespace, auth, JSON error format, pagination

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the quality of the public REST API surface in this Rails app.
EVIDENCE: code-files listing for app/controllers/api/** + config/routes.rb.
SCORE RANGE: 0-5

CRITERIA:
  C1. API controllers live under an Api:: module / app/controllers/api/ namespace.
  C2. Authentication is centralised via a before_action (e.g. require X-Auth-Token header).
  C3. Errors return a uniform JSON envelope, e.g. {"error": "<message>"}.
  C4. List endpoints support cursor-style pagination (after / before / page_after / next_cursor).
  C5. HTTP status codes are used correctly: 200/201 success, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 422 validation, 404 not-found.

SCORING ANCHORS:
  - 0 (none):       Fewer than 2 of C1-C5 satisfied; the API looks ad-hoc.
  - 2 (basic):      Exactly 2 of C1-C5; API works but inconsistent.
  - 4 (good):       3 or 4 of C1-C5; minor lapses (e.g. missing pagination on a few endpoints).
  - 5 (excellent):  All 5 of C1-C5; consistent across every controller.

OUTPUT: {"score": <0..5>, "reasoning": "<1-3 sentences referencing C1..C5>"}

nodes.description: I18n coverage: 7+ admin UI languages, 14+ signer-form languages, Rails I18n + twitter_cldr (LLM-judge, aligned with task.md §2.3 + KB-030)

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the depth of internationalisation support.
EVIDENCE: locale YAML file(s), Gemfile, application layout.
SCORE RANGE: 0-5

CONTEXT (task.md §2.3 + KB-030): The application is required to support 7 admin UI languages and 14 signing-form languages (per task.md §2.3) using Rails I18n with rails-i18n and twitter_cldr gems. The reference implementation may organize locale data as a single YAML file with multiple top-level locale keys (e.g. `en: &en`, `es: &es`, ...) using YAML anchors; this is an acceptable, idiomatic pattern.

CRITERIA:
  C1. Locale data exists under config/locales/ (one or more YAML/JSON files; single-file with multiple top-level locale anchors is acceptable).
  C2. The combined locale data covers at least 7 distinct top-level locale codes intended for the admin UI (e.g. en, es, fr, de, it, pt, nl or regional variants such as en-US/en-GB).
  C3. The combined locale data covers at least 14 distinct top-level locale codes for the signing form (e.g. additionally pl, uk, cs, he, ar, ko, ja).
  C4. Gemfile declares rails-i18n and twitter_cldr (or equivalent) gems for locale fallback and CLDR-based formatting.
  C5. The application layout / views invoke Rails I18n via t() / I18n.t helpers (not hard-coded English strings).

SCORING ANCHORS:
  - 0 (none):       0 or 1 of C1-C5 satisfied.
  - 2 (basic):      2 of C1-C5; only a handful of locales.
  - 4 (good):       3 or 4 of C1-C5; coverage is broad but a tier is missing (often C4).
  - 5 (excellent):  All 5 of C1-C5; admin and public flows are both fully localised with proper gem stack.

OUTPUT: {"score": <0..5>, "reasoning": "<1-3 sentences referencing C1..C5>"}

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the relational database design.
EVIDENCE: code-files listing for db/migrate/, db/schema.rb (or db/structure.sql) and app/models/**.

CRITERIA:
  C1. Indexes are appropriate: foreign-key indexes, unique indexes on natural keys, GIN/JSONB or tsvector indexes where needed.

CRITERIA:

nodes.description: Permission-system quality: CanCanCan ability design + account isolation + per-controller authorize_resource (LLM-judge, aligned with task.md §7 + KB-048)

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the role-based authorisation system.
EVIDENCE: ApplicationController + sample resource controllers + Ability class (or Abilities namespace).
SCORE RANGE: 0-4

CONTEXT (task.md §7 + KB-048 + KB-049): Authorization is CanCanCan-based with account-level data isolation. The Ability class may be a single `app/models/ability.rb` file OR organised as an `Abilities::*` namespace under `app/models/abilities/` (per KB-048 Abilities::TemplateConditions). admin is the only role (task.md §7.1) and users can `manage` resources within their own account (account_id-scoped). Controllers may use `load_and_authorize_resource`, `authorize_resource`, or explicit `authorize!(:action, Resource)` calls. Public endpoints opt out via `skip_authorization_check`.

CRITERIA:
  C1. ApplicationController enables CanCanCan globally (e.g. `check_authorization unless: :devise_controller?`) so authorize calls are mandatory by default.
  C2. An Ability class or Abilities namespace defines the permission matrix (admin can manage account-scoped resources; account_id condition is part of the rule).
  C3. Resource controllers invoke load_and_authorize_resource / authorize_resource / authorize! on at least 2 distinct resources (e.g. Template and Submission).
  C4. Account isolation is visibly enforced — queries are scoped via current_user.account / account_id, not global ActiveRecord.all on tenant data; public endpoints (e.g. signing form) explicitly opt out via skip_authorization_check rather than skipping silently.

SCORING ANCHORS:
  - 0 (none):       0 or 1 of C1-C4.
  - 1 (basic):      2 of C1-C4.
  - 3 (good):       3 of C1-C4.
  - 4 (excellent):  All 4 of C1-C4; tenant isolation visibly enforced.

OUTPUT: {"score": <0..4>, "reasoning": "<1-3 sentences referencing C1..C4>"}
